legend: Binary Search Search (BSS) is a cross between Breadth First Search and Binary Search. Its pseoudocode can be found below:

Even though BSS doesn't have any practical applications, you are curious as to how long it takes for this algorithm to print certain integers. More formally, you are given t$$$t$$$ testcases, each testcase containing two integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$. For each testcase, print one integer p$$$p$$$ — the position of k$$$k$$$ in the array printed by BSS.
input: The first line of input contains one integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤105$$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$) — the number of testcases. Each testcase contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ (1≤k≤n≤1018$$$1 \le k \le n \le 10^{18}$$$) — as described in the statement.
output: For each testcase, print one integer p$$$p$$$ — the position of k$$$k$$$ in the array printed by BSS.
note: For n=7$$$n=7$$$, BSS will print [4$$$4$$$ 2$$$2$$$ 6$$$6$$$ 1$$$1$$$ 3$$$3$$$ 5$$$5$$$ 7$$$7$$$]. 1$$$1$$$ is the fourth printed integer, 2$$$2$$$ is the second, 3$$$3$$$ is the fifth, 4$$$4$$$ is the first and 5$$$5$$$ is the sixth.
